c.tagline: Algeria's dramatic City of Bridges, perched over the Rhumel Gorge.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares exist but many drivers negotiate a flat price — agree it before the ride. The Yassir app is available and increasingly popular for booking cars without haggling.

emergency.note: Algeria uses 17 for police and 14 for medical emergencies; 1021 reaches civil protection (fire/rescue). English is rarely spoken by dispatchers — French or Arabic helps.

avoid.reason: Keep valuables secure in the crowded souks and around the old-town bridges; French or Arabic helps when dealing with unofficial guides.

hood_desc: The old town clinging to the rock above the Rhumel Gorge — the historic Casbah, the Souika (Swika) souk, the Souk El Ghezal Mosque and narrow Ottoman lanes; the atmospheric, must-see historic core.
The central downtown around Coudiat and the modern city with squares, cafes, colonial-era arcades and the main shopping streets; the convenient walkable base close to the bridges and transport.
A large residential and commercial district east of the gorge around the main train station, with markets, everyday eateries and mid-range hotels; a calmer, more local place to stay.
A hilltop residential quarter prized for its sweeping views over the ravine and viaducts; quiet and leafy, popular with families and those wanting a scenic, relaxed base.
The gateway quarter by the Bab El Kantara bridge linking the old rock to the newer town, near the ravine, the téléphérique station and the dramatic Sidi M'Cid bridge; close to the signature sights.

water.note: Tap water is treated but supply varies; most travelers stick to bottled.

transit.hours: The tramway and buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around 11:00 PM; the téléphérique cable car operates through the day. Taxis and the Yassir app cover late hours.
transit.note: Constantine has a modern tramway (opened 2013), a téléphérique (cable car) spanning the gorge, and an extensive city bus network, supplemented by taxis and the Yassir ride app.
transit.pay: Tram and bus fares are paid in cash (Algerian Dinar); the tram uses paper tickets validated on board. There is no unified rechargeable card across all modes as of 2026.

bus: Intercity coaches to Algiers, Annaba, Sétif and beyond
train: SNTF rail to Algiers, Annaba and Sétif from Constantine station

transit.m: Constantine tramway connects the airport line toward the city (transfer required)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for good service in restaurants and cafes is appreciated.

food.name: Chakhchoukha constantinoise
food.desc: Paper-thin rougag flatbread torn by hand into shreds and soaked in a red lamb and chickpea marqa spiced with cinnamon and dried mint.

places.name: Siniet El Bey
places.note: Traditional Constantinois table built around the city's ceremonial dishes.

places.name: Restaurant Touareg
places.note: Long-listed among Constantine's better Algerian kitchens for classic marqa dishes.

places.name: Souika family restaurants
places.note: Small family kitchens in the medina lanes cook chakhchoukha the slow, home way.

food.name: Trida
food.desc: Tiny hand-cut squares of pasta steamed and dressed with a cinnamon-scented chicken and chickpea sauce; a Constantine wedding and feast dish.

places.name: Siniet El Bey
places.note: Keeps the labour-intensive ceremonial dishes like trida and rfis on the menu.

places.name: Restaurant Mouhamed Panache
places.note: Popular local restaurant serving Algerian home-style plates at everyday prices.

places.name: Souika family restaurants
places.note: Handmade pasta dishes appear on the daily board in the medina eateries.

food.name: Mhajeb
food.desc: Semolina dough stretched translucent, folded around a cooked tomato, onion and pepper filling, then griddled flat; the street snack of choice.

places.name: Souika street stalls
places.note: Griddle counters in the covered lanes fold mhajeb to order all afternoon.

places.name: Rue Larbi Ben Mhidi snack counters
places.note: Row of cheap counters on the central shopping street, busiest at lunch.

places.name: Coudiat market stalls
places.note: Neighbourhood market griddles serving mhajeb and karantika to shoppers.

food.name: Jari and chorba frik
food.desc: Two soups the city runs on: jari, thickened with crushed wheat, and chorba frik, a tomato broth with green wheat, lamb and coriander.

places.name: Restaurant Touareg
places.note: Soups are a fixture of the traditional menu, not only during Ramadan.

places.name: Siniet El Bey
places.note: Serves jari, the old Constantinois wheat soup, alongside the celebration dishes.

places.name: Souika family restaurants
places.note: Cheapest bowls in the city, ladled from big pots at midday.

food.name: Tajine lahlou and tajine jben
food.desc: Sweet lamb tajine with prunes, cinnamon and orange-flower water, and its savoury cousin bound with fresh cheese and egg; both Constantine classics.

places.name: Siniet El Bey
places.note: Tajine jben is one of the Constantinois specialities the kitchen is known for.

places.name: Restaurant Touareg
places.note: Reliable version of the sweet prune tajine, usually a weekend dish.

places.name: Restaurant Mouhamed Panache
places.note: Home-style Algerian cooking including the sweet-savoury tajines.

food.name: Constantinois pastries
food.desc: Baklawa constantinoise heavy with almonds and honey, plus dziriette, mchewek, ktaif and griwech, made for weddings and sold by the kilo.

places.name: Rue Larbi Ben Mhidi patisseries
places.note: Window displays of honeyed pastries; the traditional place to buy by weight.

places.name: Souika sweet shops
places.note: Old medina confectioners making baklawa and ktaif by hand in small batches.

places.name: Sidi Mabrouk patisseries
places.note: Residential-quarter pastry shops used by locals for family celebrations.

food.name: Mint tea
food.desc: Green tea boiled hard with fresh mint and plenty of sugar, poured from height into small glasses and often topped with pine nuts or almonds.

places.name: Rue Larbi Ben Mhidi cafes
places.note: Pavement cafes along the main street, the city's default meeting place.

places.name: Sidi Mcid bridge cafes
places.note: Terrace cafes with the famous suspension-bridge and gorge view.

places.name: Souika tea houses
places.note: Old-quarter tea rooms where tea is drunk with pastries through the afternoon.

food.name: Sharbat
food.desc: Chilled cordials of lemon, rose or orange-flower water served at weddings and through summer, alongside fresh fruit juices and rich almond milk.

places.name: Rue Larbi Ben Mhidi patisseries
places.note: Pastry shops pour sharbat and almond drinks alongside the sweets counter.

places.name: Souika street stalls
places.note: Juice and cordial stands in the medina lanes, busiest in the heat of summer.

places.name: Coudiat market stalls
places.note: Market juice counters pressing citrus and mixing sharbat to order.

landmarks: Sidi M'Cid Bridge
Suspended 175 meters above the Rhumel gorge since 1912, this vertiginous footbridge-and-road span is the defining image of Algeria's dramatic City of Bridges.
Rhumel Gorges (Gorges du Rhumel)
The river canyon that cleaves Constantine plunges in sheer limestone walls beneath the city's bridges, threaded by a dizzying cliffside walking path.
Ahmed Bey Palace
The last great Ottoman palace built in Algeria, its arcaded courtyards, painted tiles, and orange gardens now house the national museum of arts and traditions.
Emir Abdelkader Mosque
One of Africa's largest mosques, completed in 1994, lifts twin 107-meter minarets and a vast marble prayer hall above the modern city.
Sidi Rached Viaduct
A majestic 27-arch stone viaduct completed in 1912 strides across the Rhumel valley, its 447-meter sweep among the world's great masonry bridges.
Monument aux Morts (war memorial)
Modeled on Rome's Arch of Trajan, this clifftop WWI memorial commands the single finest panorama over the gorge, bridges, and old city.
The Casbah and Souika old town
Constantine's ancient rock-top medina tumbles in whitewashed lanes, Ottoman houses, and artisan souks that have crowned the citadel since Numidian times.
Cirta National Museum
Named for the city's Numidian predecessor, this 1931 museum gathers prehistoric finds, Punic and Roman treasures, and Numidian royal artifacts from eastern Algeria.
Mellah Slimane footbridge (Passerelle Perrégaux)
A swaying 1917 pedestrian suspension bridge slung across the gorge, linking the old town to the train station in Constantine's most exhilarating short walk.
Tiddis Roman ruins
A short trip north, this striking red-rock Roman hill town cascades down terraced slopes, its arches and cisterns far from any tourist crowds.

train.note: No international trains - the Tunisian through service has not operated for years and the Moroccan border is closed. SNTF runs express trains from Constantine to Algiers in about 6 hours and to Annaba and Skikda on the coast, plus a suburban network. The station sits below the dramatic gorge that splits the city. Buy at the station or on the SNTF site.

intl.to: Tunis (Tunisia) - via the Oum Teboul or Bouchebka border
intl.op: SNTV / private Algerian operators — tickets at the Constantine bus terminal, no online booking

bus.note: Tunisia is the only open land border for travellers, reached in about 8-10 hours from Constantine. Domestic coaches run to Algiers in 6 hours, Annaba in 3 and Batna for Timgad. Buy at the terminal in cash. An Algerian visa is required in advance for most nationalities.

ferry.note: Constantine is inland, perched above the Rhumel gorge about 90 km from the sea, so there are no ferries. The nearest ports with sailings to France are Skikda and Annaba, both around two hours away by road, served by Algérie Ferries (https://www.algerieferries.dz/).

half.name: Djémila
half.blurb: A UNESCO Roman mountain city with a remarkably preserved forum, theater and triumphal arch amid rolling farmland.

half.name: Sétif
half.blurb: A regional capital with a Roman-era archaeological museum and a modern city center built around a colonial-era grid.

full.name: Timgad
full.blurb: A remarkably intact Roman colonial city known as the Pompeii of Africa, its grid of streets and arches still visible.

full.name: Annaba
full.blurb: A Mediterranean port city near the ruins of ancient Hippo Regius, where Saint Augustine once served as bishop.
